output.title: Dormant clients are a workflow problem, not a slogan
output.body:
Dormant clients look quiet, but they often leave behind a small pile of manual work: checking who has gone cold, wondering who should get a follow-up, and spending time on contact lists that never quite get reviewed. For a 1–10 person business, the real question is not whether you should “do something with AI.” It is whether re-engagement is a repeatable workflow with a clear handoff, or just a loose habit that gets done when someone remembers.

The practical decision is narrow: automate the prep work, not the judgment. That can mean flagging dormant accounts, grouping contacts by last activity, or preparing a follow-up list. The owner still decides what goes out, because any outreach that affects revenue or future contact should stay under human approval. That is the part you do not want to hand to a machine and hope for the best.

If the list is small and the review is occasional, a simple manual process is usually enough. If the same check keeps coming back every week, it is more likely a bounded automation candidate. In Bareni terms, that is the sort of workflow we would test in a free diagnostic: one recurring process, one control point, one clear measure of whether the work is worth automating.

A useful next step is to ask: which part of dormant-client follow-up takes the most time each week, the sorting or the decision? That answer usually tells you where the bottleneck really is.
